page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and its baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.e4.large operates in the lower performance tiers across multiple metrics. In processing workloads, both stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of performance. Memory bandwidth tests show a similar trend, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10%, though small-block cached reads perform slightly better in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and database operations, as measured by PassMark, also rank in the bottom 10%, while Redis SET operations achieve a weak rating in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.e4.large offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained high CPU performance. Due to its shared CPU allocation and lower benchmark scores, it is best positioned for budget-conscious, non-critical environments. Appropriate workloads include lightweight caching, basic database operations, simple web serving, and development or testing environments where compute performance is secondary to memory availability.
